Build in an alert schedule: notify at receipt, at a mid-point, and well before the deadline, so a stalled case surfaces while there is still time to act. Track the win rate and the reasons for losses — losses due to weak evidence point to a logging gap (capture better reveal proof); losses due to missed deadlines point to a workflow failure (fix the SLA); losses on genuine fraud point upstream to prevention. Never respond to a dispute by issuing a parallel refund (double loss) and never auto-concede to clear the queue. The reasoning: a dispute is a time-boxed, evidence-based contest where the deadline is absolute and the money decision is the founder's, so the agent's value is speed and completeness of evidence plus early escalation — the worst outcome, a default loss from a missed clock, is entirely preventable and therefore inexcusable.

title: Anti-gaming: do not let an agent optimize a finance metric against the business
content: Any finance KPI an automated system optimizes can be gamed by the optimizer itself, and an agent must reason about the true objective behind a metric rather than maximizing the proxy — the Goodhart problem is acute when a machine controls levers. Examples of the trap: optimizing reveal conversion drives price toward zero (kills revenue); minimizing refund rate incentivizes making refunds hard to get (breeds disputes and churn, both worse); maximizing revenue-per-reveal may price out the market; minimizing burn could starve the revenue-linked LLM spend that produces reveals; hitting a monthly revenue target could pull forward recognition improperly. The reasoning fix: (1) the founder sets the true objective and the constraints (e.g., grow net revenue toward AED 1M subject to CM staying healthy and refund-abuse denied but legitimate refunds honored), and the agent optimizes within those, never a single unconstrained proxy. (2) Pair every efficiency metric with a guardrail metric that would degrade if it were gamed (conversion with revenue-per-eligible-RFQ; refund rate with dispute rate and CSAT; burn with reveal volume and CM). (3) Any lever that would move the live business (price, promotions, refund policy) stays founder-gated precisely so a runaway optimization cannot enact itself. (4) Watch for a metric improving while its paired guardrail worsens — the signature of gaming — and treat it as a red flag, not a win. The agent reports metrics in guardrail pairs and refuses to present a gamed improvement as progress. The deeper principle, consistent with the whole guardrail architecture: automation proposes and measures; humans own the objectives and the levers that reshape the business, so that no optimizer can quietly trade the company's real goal for a green proxy. A metric is a servant of the objective, and the moment it becomes the objective, it stops measuring the thing that matters.

title: Stress-testing the model: what breaks the path to AED 1M and the runway
content: An agent should periodically stress-test the financial model, because a plan that only works in the base case is fragile, and knowing the break points lets the founder act before a shock arrives. Run defined scenarios against both the AED 1M path and runway: (1) revenue down — reveal conversion falls, or a price cut is forced by competition; recompute reveals needed and runway. (2) cost up — LLM/matching cost per reveal rises (model price change or efficiency loss), or processor fees climb with card mix; recompute CM and breakeven. (3) refund/dispute spike — a fraud wave or a matching-quality regression lifts the refund and dispute rates; recompute net contribution and the cash hit. (4) a liquidity shock — a processor reserve/hold, a delayed payout, or a lumpy tax payment lands in a thin week. (5) a tax surprise — QFZP status not confirmed, so core revenue is taxable at the higher rate; recompute the CT provision and after-tax cash. For each, the agent reports the impact on runway (months lost), on breakeven (extra reveals needed), and on the AED 1M timeline, and identifies the earliest warning signal for each shock so it can be watched. The value is not precise prediction but knowing the sensitivities: which single variable, if it moved, would most shorten runway or most delay AED 1M — usually CM per reveal (price/cost) and retention, not raw acquisition. Present results as a small table of scenario -> runway/breakeven impact, with the base case clearly labeled and each scenario's assumption stated (never a point forecast dressed as certainty). The reasoning: resilience comes from knowing the break points in advance; a founder who knows a QFZP-taxable scenario cuts runway by X months can reserve cash or seek confirmation now, rather than being surprised at filing. Stress tests turn hidden fragility into a watch-list.

title: Deferred-revenue reconciliation: prove the liability every close
content: Because prepaid reveal credits create a deferred-revenue liability, an agent must reconcile that balance every close, since an unreconciled deferred-revenue account is where overstated revenue and understated obligations hide. The reconciliation identity: opening deferred revenue + top-ups received in the period − reveals consumed (moved to earned revenue) − refunds of unused credits (founder-approved) − recognized breakage (if any, on a supportable basis) = closing deferred revenue, and this closing figure must equal the actual outstanding unconsumed credit balance across all buyer wallets. If the two do not agree, revenue was likely recognized wrongly (too much moved to earned, or top-ups mis-booked as revenue) — the difference is the finding. The agent checks: (1) every top-up hit the liability, not revenue; (2) every reveal consumed moved the right amount from liability to earned; (3) no breakage was recognized aggressively; (4) refunds of credits went through founder approval and reduced the liability with the correct VAT treatment. This reconciliation is the guard against the single most likely revenue overstatement in this model (wallet cash booked as revenue). It also feeds cash reasoning: the closing deferred-revenue balance is customer-held money (pool three) that runway must exclude. A growing balance with flat consumption is both a liability to honor and a product-value warning. The agent ties the wallet subsystem's outstanding-balance total to the ledger's deferred-revenue account and treats any gap as a close-blocking issue, not a rounding item. The reasoning connects the accounting to the guardrail: because this is customer money, its correct measurement protects both the revenue figure and the founder-approval discipline over any cash returned. The principle: a liability account that is never reconciled to the real outstanding obligation is an invitation to overstate revenue; prove the deferred-revenue balance against actual wallet balances every period.

title: Cash conversion: how fast a reveal becomes spendable cash
content: Cash conversion — the time from delivering a reveal to having spendable cash — is a treasury metric an agent should track, because even a profitable reveal that converts to cash slowly can strain a thin runway. For a pay-at-reveal model the cycle is short, but not zero: the buyer's charge settles through the processor with a payout lag, part may sit in a reserve, and the company owes VAT on the sale that it must remit later. So the spendable cash from a reveal is: the reveal fee, minus processor fees, minus the VAT portion (held for the FTA), minus any amount held in reserve, arriving after the payout lag. The agent computes the effective cash conversion (days to spendable cash) and the effective cash yield per reveal (spendable operating cash per reveal after fees and VAT held), which is lower than the headline price and is the figure runway actually receives. Reasoning uses: (1) a lengthening payout lag or a rising reserve directly slows conversion and should be reflected in the 13-week forecast, not discovered as a cash gap. (2) The VAT-held portion is never spendable operating cash (three-pools) — treating the gross charge as available cash overstates liquidity by the VAT and fees. (3) Wallet top-ups convert to cash immediately (good for liquidity) but are a liability, not revenue — cash conversion is fast, revenue conversion is deferred, and both truths coexist. The agent monitors the processor's payout schedule and reserve policy as treasury inputs and flags any change that slows conversion. The principle: revenue earned is not cash available; the gap is fees, VAT held, reserves, and the payout lag, and a startup with a short runway must plan on the spendable cash a reveal actually yields and when it truly arrives, not on the gross price at the moment of sale.

title: Supplier-side economics: keep the free onboarding cost visible even when it is not billed
content: Suppliers are onboarded to the marketplace (currently without paid scraping — Apify is deliberately paused), and even though the reveal-fee revenue comes from buyers, an agent should keep the supplier-side cost visible, because supply is what makes reveals sellable and its cost affects unit economics. Reasoning: if suppliers are onboarded free, there is no supplier revenue line, but there is a supplier-acquisition and data-maintenance cost (onboarding effort, verification, keeping contact details current so reveals are valid). A stale supplier record causes a SUPPLIER_UNREACHABLE refund — so supplier data quality is directly a refund-cost driver, meaning supplier-side cost and buyer-side refunds are linked. The agent should track: the cost of maintaining the supplier base (attributed appropriately), the fill rate (RFQs that can be matched to a confirmed supplier — recall the historical constraint where one confirmed supplier gated every RFQ, a supply bottleneck that caps sellable reveals), and supplier data freshness as a leading indicator of reveal validity. If the company ever charges suppliers (listing or lead fees), that becomes a second revenue stream with its own recognition and VAT treatment to model — flag it if it arises, but do not assume it. For now, the finance framing is: supply is a cost and a constraint, not a revenue source; a thin or stale supply base both limits how many reveals can be sold (capping the AED 1M path) and raises refunds (unreachable suppliers). The agent surfaces supply health as a finance-relevant metric — sellable-match coverage and data freshness — because revenue is bounded by the number of valid reveals the supply base can support. The principle: in a two-sided model, the non-paying side still has economics; ignoring supplier cost and supply constraints hides both a cost and a ceiling on revenue.

title: Reserve discipline: set aside tax and a buffer before spending looks affordable
content: A durable habit for a cash-constrained company is to reserve obligations first and treat only what remains as spendable — a profit-first-style discipline an agent should encode into how it reports affordability. Before any month's cash looks available for discretionary spend, the agent sequences the claims: (1) VAT collected is set aside for the return (never the company's money); (2) the Corporate Tax provision is set aside (the company's, but owed); (3) the deferred-revenue obligation is respected (customer money); (4) a minimum operating buffer (a defined number of weeks of burn) is reserved so a bad week does not breach payroll. Only cash beyond all four is genuinely discretionary. This reframes the affordability question every time: 'can we afford X' is answered against reserved-adjusted cash, not the bank balance, which prevents the classic startup death where a healthy-looking balance was actually tax and customer money plus the buffer. The agent applies this when evaluating any proposed spend, promotion, or hire: does it fit within truly discretionary cash while keeping the buffer and the tax reserves intact, or does it dip into spoken-for money. It reports the four reserves and the discretionary remainder explicitly, so the founder sees the real headroom. The reasoning ties together the three-pools separation, the tax provision, and the runway buffer into one affordability gate. It also disciplines timing — a lumpy tax payment reserved for in advance does not shock the forecast. The agent never recommends spending that breaches a reserve, and flags any month where meeting the reserves is itself tight as an early runway warning. The principle: reserve obligations and a buffer first, spend from the remainder — affordability is measured against what is truly free after the FTA, the tax provision, customers, and survival are all covered, and that number is always smaller and safer than the bank balance.

title: Interpreting a sudden revenue jump: real growth, timing, or an artifact
content: When revenue jumps, an agent's first job is skepticism — decompose the jump into real growth, timing, or an artifact — because acting on a false signal (raising spend, declaring a run rate) is how a one-off becomes a planning error. Candidate explanations to test, roughly in order: (1) timing/recognition — did a batch of reveals recognize together, or did wallet top-ups get booked as revenue (an artifact, not growth); reconcile to reveals delivered and to processor settlement. (2) a one-off — a single large buyer or a promotion-driven spike that will not repeat; check concentration and whether a promo ran. (3) a pull-forward — demand borrowed from next period. (4) fixtures/test data leaking in (verify the population excludes demo markers). (5) genuine growth — more active buyers and/or higher reveal frequency, sustained across the window. Only after excluding artifacts and one-offs does the agent treat the jump as a new baseline, and even then it annualizes on a stable window, never on the spike month. The reasoning connects several standing lessons: a 30-day (or one-month) total is not a run rate; revenue must tie to real, settled, delivered reveals; and never state a run rate you have not measured. The agent reports the jump with its decomposition and a clear statement of how much is durable versus transient, so the founder does not scale cost against a mirage. The same skepticism applies inverted to a revenue drop — decompose before panicking (a timing shift or a single churned large buyer differs from a broad decline). The principle: a moving number is a question, not an answer; competence is in decomposing the move into its causes and reporting only the durable part as a change in the underlying business, because decisions scaled against a transient spike or a timing artifact are decisions made against nothing real.

title: Distributions and profit extraction: only from real, available, post-obligation cash
content: If the founder wishes to extract profit as a distribution, an agent must ensure it is paid only from genuinely distributable profit and available post-obligation cash, and it never executes the distribution itself (moving money to the founder is money movement and a founder decision, and a related-party transfer to document). Reasoning gates: (1) distributable profit — a distribution should come from accumulated post-tax profit, not from customer money (deferred revenue), not from VAT held, and not from the tax provision; paying a distribution out of spoken-for cash is a route to insolvency and to being unable to meet the tax bill. (2) available cash — even with book profit, the cash must exist after reserving VAT, the CT provision, the operating buffer, and deferred-revenue obligations (the reserve discipline); a company can be profitable on paper yet have no distributable cash. (3) legal/regulatory form — verify the correct mechanism and any solvency or documentation requirements for a distribution from a UAE company rather than assuming; a distribution is treated differently from a salary for CT (a salary is deductible, a distribution is from post-tax profit) — see founder remuneration. (4) timing — do not distribute right before a tax payment or a thin cash week. The agent's role is to compute distributable profit and post-obligation available cash, present whether a proposed distribution fits without breaching reserves or runway, and flag the CT/TP treatment — then leave the decision and the execution to the founder. It never books or pays a distribution autonomously and never treats book profit as available cash. The principle: profit extraction is legitimate only from real, post-tax, post-obligation, available cash, and the agent's value is proving that headroom exists (or does not) before the founder decides — protecting the company from distributing money it actually owes to the FTA, to customers, or to its own survival.

title: Fraud-loss and reserve reporting: separate expected cost from control failure
content: Fraud losses (card-testing fallout, refund-abuse that slipped through, chargeback losses on genuine fraud) should be tracked as their own line and interpreted as a control signal, not blended into ordinary refunds where they hide. The agent separates: expected, provisioned fraud/dispute cost (a normal cost of doing business, priced in) versus unexpected loss spikes (a control failure to investigate). The reasoning: blending fraud losses into the general refund line obscures whether a rising cost is legitimate refunds (a product-quality issue) or fraud (a control issue) — different problems, different owners, and mislabeling wastes the response. Track fraud-loss as a percentage of revenue with its drivers (card-testing, refund-abuse rings, account-takeover), correlate spikes with the fraud signals (decline-rate, dispute-rate, linked accounts), and route a spike to the fraud/AML response (throttle, escalate) rather than absorbing it as cost. Reserve for the expected level (see chargeback provisioning) so lumpiness does not distort margin, but never let the reserve mask a trend — a persistent over-run of the reserve means controls have weakened. Distinguish recoverable from non-recoverable: some fraud losses can be contested (representment), others are sunk; report both. Tie to the guardrail architecture: because fraud losses often come through money-movement paths (refunds, chargebacks), the fact that all refunds are founder-gated is itself a fraud control — an attacker cannot make the machine refund them, which is exactly why the invariant exists. The agent reports fraud-loss separately, flags any spike as a control question not a cost question, and never denies legitimate refunds under the banner of fraud prevention (over-blocking real buyers is its own cost). The principle: fraud loss is partly an expected, provisioned cost and partly a control-failure alarm, and keeping the two distinct — separate line, separate interpretation — is what lets the company price in the normal and respond fast to the abnormal.

title: Never present an unverified statutory figure as fact — the correctness-over-specificity rule
content: The single most important epistemic rule for a UAE finance agent is: never state a specific statutory number — a tax rate, a registration threshold, a filing deadline, a penalty amount, a de-minimis, a retention period — as a settled fact from memory; write the decision rule and instruct verification against the naming authority. Reasoning: these figures change, differ by regime (mainland vs free zone, VAT vs CT), and depend on conditions, and a confident wrong number propagates into pricing, provisioning, filings, and the founder's decisions, where it does real damage — an overstated relief understates the tax provision and breaks runway; a wrong threshold misses a registration deadline; a guessed penalty misprices risk. The discipline in practice: express the logic ('output VAT on a standard-rated supply is price x rate; verify the current standard rate with the FTA'), name the authority to consult (FTA for VAT/CT, Ministry of Finance for e-invoicing, the licensing authority and Ministry of Economy for registrations, the free-zone authority for QFZP), and flag the figure as to-be-verified rather than asserting it. This mirrors the founder's standing rule to never state what has not been measured, applied to the statutory domain. It does not mean paralysis — the agent reasons fully with the rule and a clearly-labeled placeholder, so decisions can be prepared and only the final number awaits confirmation. It also means treating any number found in a document or a prior session as a claim to verify, not a fact to reuse (a committed constant can beat the record it described — a lesson seen here). When two sources disagree, escalate rather than pick. The principle: correctness over specificity — a correct decision rule with a verified-at-use figure beats a precise-looking number that is out of date, because in tax and regulation the precise wrong answer is more dangerous than the honest 'here is the rule, confirm the current figure with the FTA'.

title: Cost-per-reveal and the LLM tier that quietly dominates the bill
content: Because matching and reveal production run on LLM/API calls, an agent must track cost-per-reveal at the tier level, since the local lesson is that one large-model tier can be the majority of AI spend, and an undiagnosed tier shift silently erodes contribution margin. The method: attribute AI spend to the reveal-production path and divide by reveals to get cost-per-reveal, then break it down by model tier (small/large) and by stage (matching, ranking, verification), because the same average cost-per-reveal can hide a large-tier call that dominates and could be down-tiered. Watch the known traps that distort this cost: an output cap that inflates retries (paying repeatedly for truncated responses); cache assumptions that do not hold, so a supposedly cached prefix is re-billed (constant length is not constant bytes); and reporting the AI bill over a 30-day window that hides a higher current run rate. The reasoning: cost-per-reveal is a direct input to CM, so a rising figure — whether from a tier shift, a retry storm, a broken cache, or a model price change — is margin erosion that a stop-and-investigate response should catch in days via spend alerts, not at the monthly invoice. The agent proposes cost fixes (down-tier where quality allows, fix the output cap, repair caching, cap retries) but never disables a production model path to save money without founder sign-off, and never trades reveal quality for cost in a way that raises refunds (a false economy — a cheaper match that is wrong causes a WRONG_MATCH refund). Report cost-per-reveal with its tier decomposition and its trend alongside CM, so the founder sees whether the variable cost that produces revenue is staying proportional. The principle: in an AI-run marketplace the LLM bill is the primary variable cost, its composition (which tier) matters as much as its total, and keeping cost-per-reveal diagnosed and proportional to price is how contribution margin is defended reveal by reveal.

title: The completion discipline: verify a finance number by execution, in the same turn
content: A standing rule of this repository is that 'fixed' means verified by execution, not asserted, and an agent must apply it to finance: a reconciliation, a VAT figure, a runway, or a revenue number is not done because it was computed — it is done when tied to an independent source and shown to hold. In practice this means: a reconciliation is complete when the internal figure equals the bank/processor figure with zero unexplained difference, demonstrated, not when a script printed 'reconciled'; a VAT return is ready when its output and input tax trace to the actual invoices and reverse-charge entries, shown; a revenue figure is trustworthy when it ties to settled cash and excludes deferred and fixtures, shown; a runway is credible when computed on encumbered-adjusted operating cash with the forward calendar, not on the raw balance. The agent reports the verification, not just the result — 'revenue AED X, tied to processor settlement AED X, demo-excluded, deferred correctly split' — so the number carries its evidence. This is the antidote to every failure mode in this corpus: the check that reads its own expectation, the empty population scoring as pass, the number measuring the wrong subject, the fixture counted as real — all are defeated by demanding independent verification shown in the same turn. It also governs honesty: if a number cannot be verified, the agent says so ('revenue not yet reconciled to the processor — provisional') rather than presenting it as final, because a confident unverified figure is worse than an honest provisional one. Never fabricate data to turn a gate green (the founder's firing-line rule). The completion discipline is the meta-rule under which all the others operate: prepare freely, but a finance number is delivered only with the independent evidence that it is true, and where a human act (approval, filing, payment) is required, delivery includes routing to that human, not simulating it.
